title: auth: clarify header semantics for project/org keys, scoped tokens, CORS, and request signing (OpenAI-compat)
author: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Align and document Authorization and auxiliary header semantics across the Redwood API and the OpenAI-compat layer. This PR unifies behavior for project keys vs org keys, introduces clear handling for scoped tokens, formalizes CORS preflight/credentials behavior for browser clients, and implements a light-weight request signing header pair (X-Redwood-Nonce + X-Redwood-Signature) for optional anti-replay verification.
Motivation: Several customers and SDKs have encountered ambiguous behavior when mixing project-scoped and org-scoped API keys, and the OpenAI-compat shim exposed inconsistent header handling (especially around Authorization + X-Project vs X-Org-ID headers and CORS). This caused streaming and function-calling clients running in browsers to fail due to preflight rejections or missing credential forwarding.
Changes:
- Normalize precedence: Authorization bearer token (scoped or org/project) is primary. If present, X-Redwood-Project and X-Redwood-Org headers are advisory and are validated against token scope; if they conflict with token scope the request is rejected (401).
- Add support for scoped tokens: token metadata (scope) is validated at the API gateway and propagated via X-Redwood-Caller-Scope for internal services.
- CORS/browser behavior: clarified and implemented Access-Control-Allow-Credentials and Access-Control-Allow-Headers handling for streaming endpoints; preflight will now explicitly allow Authorization, X-Redwood-Nonce, X-Redwood-Signature, X-Project, and X-Org-ID.
- Optional request signing: new pair of optional headers (X-Redwood-Nonce and X-Redwood-Signature) for customers wanting anti-replay on pubic clients. Signature verification can be toggled per-project. Nonce replay will return 401 with hint header X-Redwood-Nonce-Status.
- OpenAI-compat layer: ensure legacy OpenAI-style X-OpenAI-Organization header is mapped to X-Redwood-Org-ID and validated consistently. Old behavior where X-Project header silently overrode bearer token scope is removed.
- SDK and docs: python/ts SDKs now expose helper to attach nonce/signature; docs updated with examples for CORS, browser streaming, and function-calling flows that require scoped tokens.
- Tests & CI: unit + integration tests added for token precedence, CORS preflight, and signature validation.
Checklist:
- [x] API gateway validation logic implemented
- [x] Signature verification implementation behind feature flag per-project
- [x] OpenAI-compat header mapping added
- [x] SDK helpers (py/ts) added and tests updated
- [x] Documentation and migration notes included
- [x] E2E tests for streaming + browser preflight added
Related: Linear ENG-4821 (auth header spec), ENG-4910 (browser streaming fixes), PM-223 (OpenAI compat parity). Links: internal design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/auth-header-spec

Notes/compat: This change is backwards-compatible by default: existing bearer tokens continue working. Projects opting into strict signing or strict header validation will need to enable the per-project flag and rotate clients to send nonces/signatures. Rolling plan: gate signature verification behind per-project toggle, default mapping behavior available immediately.

release_notes: Clarified Authorization header semantics: token precedence enforced, explicit CORS preflight allowances for Authorization and signing headers, optional per-project request-signing (X-Redwood-Nonce + X-Redwood-Signature) behind feature flag, OpenAI-compat header mapping fixed. SDKs updated with helpers; migration docs added.
